summary: The FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) was signed into law by President Barack Obama on January 4, 2011. It gave the Food and Drug Administration new authority to regulate how foods are grown, harvested and processed, including mandatory recall authority the agency had long sought. The law also requires the FDA to carry out more than a dozen rulemakings and issue at least 10 guidance documents, along with many reports, plans, strategies, standards and notices.
one_line: Overview of the 2011 Food Safety Modernization Act, which expanded FDA authority over food growing, harvesting and processing.
key_facts: The Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) was signed into law by President Barack Obama on January 4, 2011.
The FSMA gave the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) new authorities to regulate the way foods are grown, harvested and processed.
The FSMA grants the FDA mandatory recall authority.
The FDA had sought mandatory recall authority for many years before the FSMA granted it.
The FSMA requires the FDA to undertake more than a dozen rulemakings.
The FSMA requires the FDA to issue at least 10 guidance documents.
The FSMA requires the FDA to produce a host of reports, plans, strategies, standards, notices, and other tasks.
